Subject: Dedicated capacity — help picking H100 vs A100 vs L4?

Hi Markus,

Quick intro: I run infra at AuroraAI (cc'd procurement). We're moving a production retrieval+RAG stack to dedicated capacity and trying to pick the right GPU mix. Primary constraints: 1) 30–60k tokens/session tail cases, 2) a lot of short chat traffic (<1k tokens) for metadata queries, 3) cost sensitivity — want to keep unit token spend reasonable.

We asked our engineers to profile a few models; results are noisy (vary by context length). Can you advise when to pick H100 vs A100 vs L4 for Dedicated, and what a pragmatic pilot fleet looks like? Also, what are the ops tradeoffs (fallbacks, cache strategy) we should budget for?

If helpful I attached a small CSV with a couple of sample traces (aurora_profile_template.csv). Could we get a short recommended pilot plan and a spec we can run in our PoC next week?

Thanks,
Timothy Hayes
Head of Infrastructure, AuroraAI

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — help picking H100 vs A100 vs L4?

Timothy — thanks for the context and the trace. Looping in Kim (SE) and Connor (Solutions) for sizing and ops notes. High level guidance up front:

- H100: pick for very large-context models or heavy multi-query long-context RAG where KV cache and memory footprint are the dominant constraint. Best for 30k+ token persistent state and models that need large activations.
- A100: good middle ground — excellent throughput for batch/steady-state inference, lower unit cost than H100 for many medium-context workloads, but less headroom for extreme sequence lengths.
- L4: cost-efficient for short-context, high-concurrency front-ends and asymmetric traffic. Great for embedding/bulk p99 < 1k token use cases and for overprovisioning cheap slots for spikes.

Recommendation pattern: start with a small H100 pool to serve long-context models + KV caching, pair with a larger L4 pool for front-door short-token traffic, and use A100s as the predictable throughput layer for mid-size workloads where batching helps.

Next steps: Kim/Connor — can you take the CSV, run a quick fitment and propose a 30-day pilot config (initial nodes, fallback policy, cost ballpark, per-token estimates)? Tim — I'll send a short summary back to you and include an ops playbook for canary.

-Markus

Timothy / team — I ran the traces through our quick-fit tool and attached a compact fitment matrix (fitment-matrix.xlsx) and a one-page summary (h100-vs-a100-l4-summary.pdf). Key points below:

1) Memory vs perf thresholds
- If median context > 8k tokens or > 24GB KV per model instance, default to H100 for primary serving. Example: your RAG index shard with heavy long-history sessions.
- For stable throughput where batching can be leveraged (>50 concurrency with predictable patterns), A100 yields better $/token.
- L4 is optimal for conversational front-door and embedding workloads where context < 2k and latency budgets are tight (~50–100ms).

2) Pilot sizing (30-day PoC baseline)
- H100: 4x slots dedicated to long-context model (reserve for peak long sessions; use autoscale thresholds)
- A100: 8x slots to handle mid-context inference and batch jobs (can be scaled incrementally)
- L4: 24x slots for front-door short contexts and burst capacity
Estimated blended cost: ~X tokens-per-dollar equivalent (ballpark attached). Exact numbers in fitment-matrix.xlsx.

3) Ops/playbook highlights
- Enable prefix/KV caching on H100 pool; set TTLs based on session telemetry and early eviction for stale shards.
- Routing policy: prefer H100 by model tag for long-context model_ids, fallback to A100 only if latency SLO can be relaxed, fallback to L4 only for short-context polyfills.
- Canary: run 10% traffic through pilot H100 pool for 72 hours, monitor cache hit rate and tail latency.

Attachments: fitment-matrix.xlsx, h100-vs-a100-l4-summary.pdf

-Kim

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — ops notes and fallback patterns

Adding a few ops-specific items and a concrete fallback plan we use with Dedicated customers.

- Fallback tiers:
  1) Primary: H100 pool tagged long-context (strict latency SLO)
  2) Secondary: A100 pool for relaxed p95 targets and batched workloads
  3) Tertiary: L4 pool for short-context polyfills and best-effort workloads

- Pre-warm and slot sizing: pre-warm KV caches on H100 for known hot shards; if you have predictable shard-to-user mappings, pin those shards to slots to avoid cold-starting KV loads.

- Tiling and tiling fallback: for extremely long sessions we recommend checkpointing the KV cache so sessions can be tiled across H100s without re-compute; control tiling from the router by model version.

- Monitoring: expose per-model KV-hit-rate, per-slot memory headroom, and cross-pool fallthrough counts. Automate a scale-up if H100 slot utilization > 70% for > 15 minutes.

Pilot concrete numbers (ops-friendly):
- Start: 4 H100, 6 A100, 16 L4
- Canary: route 5% of production traffic for 72h, then 20% for one week, then open to full if tail latencies match SLOs.

I'll add an ops checklist to the HubSpot deal page and link infra-runbooks.

-Connor
